verifier: Commons file pages read for this pass. Not an independent legal opinion.
processing: Each file was redrawn to grayscale, given a light grain, cover-cropped to 500×700, and saved as JPEG with an APP0 marker only. No EXIF, GPS, APP1 or APP13.
cache: These JPEGs are not in the service-worker precache. The first request for a card's photo is stored by the existing runtime cache, so a photo already shown still loads offline. The first install does not download the pool.
gaps: Marx: four photographs. Later prints, rotations and colourisations of the same sittings were not counted.
Engels: five photographs. The coloured 1891 file was not used, because a tint is not a new photograph.

Mao Zedong in 1924.jpg is a colourised picture and was not used. Mao Zedong (1920) 02.jpg looked like a closer crop of the 1920 portrait and was not used. Yan'an group file looked colourised and was not used.
Photograph of Mao Zedong with Evans Carlson circa 1937.jpg was downloaded and is a different sitting, but its licence template was not re-read after a Commons rate limit, so it is excluded.

Castro pool is one photograph. Excluded: Montreal 1959 (tagged Not-PD-US-URAA and PD-Canada); UN General Assembly 1960 (PD-USNWR plus Copyright-tag-still-required); Augusto Martinez Sanchez 1960 (PD-Cuba, not confirmed to cover this photograph); 1972 Prague (PD-CzechGov, not confirmed to cover this photograph). Poster and mural files were not used.

Kim Il Sung: three photographs. Excluded: Kim Il-sung Portrait.jpg (a 2019 photograph of a portrait, CC BY 2.5, not a sitting); Poland 1956 (credit URL on the file was a reddit link); Kim Il-sung 1946.JPG (PD-Japan-oldphoto while the stated source was Korean People Journal); the 1948 group photograph (a crowd, and a weak portrait); Kim Il-sung 1958.jpg (about 123 px wide).

PD-North Korea and PD-1996 are the Commons tags printed on those Kim files. This pass did not get a separate legal opinion. Reviewers who do not accept those tags should drop kim-1946.jpg and kim-1950.jpg.
Karl Marx 001.jpg uses a generic {{PD}} template. The file names John Jabez Edwin Mayall and a date before 24 August 1875, and LicenseShortName was Public domain.
Some files were fetched through Commons at a maximum width of 1400 px. fetchedPixels is that download, not always the master scan.
Lenin 1921 and some other scans are smaller than 500×700. They were not invented up to a false sharpness; the JPEG is soft.
No crop, flip or tint of one photograph was given a second id.
